newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - March 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - March 13.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Government introduces special emergency regulations to shut down illegal video parlours saying they offended public morality and corrupted young children.

Chinese government releases 14 Sri Lankan illegal immigrants in a goodwill gesture, Foreign Ministry spokesman says. They were arrested by Chinese authorities last week with forged passports at Guangzhou.

Opposition MP Anura Bandaranaike, estranged brother of President Chandrika Kumaratunga, claims 25 million rupees as compensation from government for an alleged arbitrary search of his house by police last month. Police searched Bandaranike's Colombo house on suspicion he was hiding an opposition MP wanted by police for the killing of a ruling coalition legislator.
Government enacts new laws under emergency regulations to crack down on those using illegal firearms, enabling authorities to confiscate houses or vehicles in which illegal firearms are found.

Ferrying of Tamil refugees by separatist Tamil rebels has temporarily been halted after a boat carrying refugees capsized in the northern seas last month killing nearly 130 people, Indian boatsmen in police custody say.

Main opposition United National Party members file false complaints on violence against them to win sympathy from voters, President Kumaratunga tells election rally. Over 1,000 incidents of election-related violence have been reported during the past month.
